To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of a small left heart ventricular cavity in the second trimester of pregnancy is associated with a high incidence of fetal anomalies.
the incidence of extracardioc defects in fetuses with a small left ventricular cavity is high.
the presence of a small left heart ventricles in a fetus with a normal proximal outlet tract has an extremely poor prognosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for the detection and classification of anomalies in fetal echocardiographic images.
the study of the effects of the presence of a small left heart ventricles.
the development and evaluation of a novel, non‐invasive technique to detect and monitor the presence of the fetal small left heart ventricular outflow tract obstruction (SLV‐OT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a small left ventricular cavity in the second trimester fetus is associated with a poor outcome, and termination of pregnancy is recommended.

(1) a small left ventricular volume is not an indication for termination of pregnancy; (2) the presence of associated anomalies, particularly coarctation and an abnormal karyotype, is an indication for termination; and (3) in cases of a left ventricular hypoplasia, the presence of a small left atrium is a strong indication for termination of the pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diagnosis of small left ventricles with normal outflow tract in the second trimester is associated with a high incidence of associated abnormalities.

the presence of a small left heart ventricular volume in early pregnancy is a strong indication for further fetal echocardiographic and anatomic investigations, since the prognosis for the fetus is poor.
the presence of a small left heart ventricles in the first trimester of gestation is an indicator of a high risk pregnancy and should prompt a detailed fetal echocardiographic examination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a small left heart ventricule with a normal proximal outlet tract in early pregnancy may be a marker of fetal aneuploidy or other major structural abnormalities.
a small left heart ventricular cavity with a normal out flow tract can be detected early in pregnancy by ultrasound.

the small left ventricles with normal outflow tracts detected on prenatal ultrasound are associated with a high incidence of other fetal abnormalities, including coarctation and chromosomal aberrations.
